thread:
tyler_sales: Heads up team — Nimbus Labs POC hit a hard stop during a demo. Calls to /generate are returning 403 invalid_project_claim even though the customer says the key is "active" in their vault. Need fast triage.

devx_maya: Paste the exact curl + raw JSON error and any request_id.

tyler_sales: They pasted this: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_nimbus_77' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -H 'X-Redwood-Org: nimbus-labs' \n  -H 'X-Redwood-Project: nimbus-test' \n  -d '{"model":"rw/gpt-9b","input":"status"}'```
Raw response: `\{\"error\":\"invalid_project_claim\",\"status\":403,\"hint\":\"jwt project claim= nimbus-core != header nimbus-test\",\"request_id\":\"req-nimbus-2026-700\"\}`

li_eng: Hint makes it clear — JWT claim is nimbus-core but header is nimbus-test. Likely they used an older/global key or a key from a different project.

tyler_sales: Customer insists they copied the key from the "nimbus-test" project page. They have one engineer on the call.

ops_jordan: We tightened header enforcement last month. Pre-policy global keys will 403 on mismatched headers. If rotation is hard for them, we can request a short-lived routing exception, but that requires change control (~2h).

devx_maya: Fastest remediation is rotate/create a new project-scoped key: Console -> Projects -> nimbus-test -> Keys -> Create. Ask them to swap the key and retry. Temporary (not recommended) workaround: remove X-Redwood-Project header so gateway falls back to token claim.

li_eng: Also ask them to decode the JWT header+payload and paste only the payload (no signature) or give us the request_id so we decode server-side. Example snippet to decode payload (redact signature): `python -c "import base64,json; p='<token>'.split('.')[1]; print(json.dumps(json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(p+'==')), indent=2))"`

tyler_sales: They also mentioned intermittent 429s earlier when demo clients retried rapidly. If we fix auth and they replay failed requests we'll see another spike. Can ops grant a short quota bump?

ops_jordan: For demos we can temporarily bump project quotas: burst=100, steady=10rps for 24h. I'll apply and audit it in the ticket.

li_eng: Dev tip to pass to their engineer: ensure token claims and headers match. Node example: `fetch(url, { headers: { 'Authorization':'Bearer sk_...', 'X-Redwood-Org':'nimbus-labs', 'X-Redwood-Project':'nimbus-core' } })`

tyler_sales: They're also completing an RFP SQ — asking about rotation cadence, RBAC, and audit logs. Any short copy I can send?

ops_jordan: SQ blurb: "We support project-scoped API keys, console/API-based rotation, RBAC via org/project scoping, and audit logs. For Private customers we offer KMS/HSM integration and configurable rotation policies. Recommended rotation cadence is customer-defined (30-90 days typical)." Attach SOC2 & docs on request.

devx_maya: If they want sustained throughput, sales should propose a 30-day Dedicated trial. That gives predictable capacity and avoids quota juggling. Tyler, ping Sam for quote.

tyler_sales: Will do. I've opened a support ticket with request_id=req-nimbus-2026-700. Please assign to eng-triage and note the temporary quota bump.

support-bot: support-bot: ticket #SUP-2026-610 created for req-nimbus-2026-700, assigned eng-triage.

li_eng: Standing by to decode JWT or escalate for routing exception if rotation fails.

tyler_sales: Thanks all — I'm telling the customer to rotate their key and hold off on replays until we confirm quota bump. I'll post the new curl here when they swap. :thumbsup:
